crusader_leaders_regard.description: Standing among the other crusade princes (Godfrey, Raymond, Robert of Normandy, and others) - a council of rivals as much as allies.

byzantine_relations.description: Relations with Emperor Alexios I Komnenos - fraught from the start, and central to almost everything the expedition does logistically.

army_morale.description: Morale and cohesion of your own contingent specifically.

church_favor.description: Standing with the Church and the papal legate's authority over the expedition.

popular_support.description: Standing with the rank-and-file pilgrims and soldiers of the wider host, beyond your own men.

treasury.description: Coin and supply on hand - a real, constant constraint on a campaign this far from home.

territorial_ambition.description: Concrete progress toward carving out a personal territorial foothold in the East - deliberately low to start; this is the resource the Antioch arc is built to move.

foreign_reputation.description: Reputation and diplomatic standing with regional Muslim powers (Seljuk, Fatimid, and local emirates) - relevant to negotiation as much as war.

personal_safety.description: Physical safety on campaign - sieges, disease, and ambush are all real threats this far from home.

notes: Starting values reflect June 1097: Nicaea has just fallen to the crusaders (and been handed to Alexios rather than sacked, a real point of crusader resentment), the army is marching into Anatolia, and the siege of Antioch - the campaign's central Bohemond-flavored arc - is still ahead.
